newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus exchange halts trade in cement industries.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus exchange halts trade in cement industries.

text.p: Cyprus's stock exchange has halted trading in two cement companies for issuing contradictory statements on share transactions between them, its director said on Tuesday.
Trading in Vassiliko Cement Works and Cyprus Cement has been halted for two days after one company announced buying a huge block of shares in the other, and the latter subsequently denying it.
"We want to get the full picture, the true facts," Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters.
"The board of the exchange is due to meet on the issue. If the answers we get are not satisfactory this (suspension) will continue," he said.
The dispute was sparked when Cyprus Cement announced on the floor on Monday that it had agreed to purchase shares worth 35 million pounds ($75 million) in Vassiliko.
The deal, which Cyprus Cement said was made with Archbishop Chrysostomos of the Greek Orthodox church as a major shareholder in Vassiliko, was almost immediately disputed.

Vassiliko simultaneously announced a deal with Companie Financiere et de Participations, a member of Italcementi of Italy for the purchase of 5.588.552 fully paid shares representing 13 percent of its issued capital.
Vassiliko, which is partly owned by the Greek Orthodox Church of Cyprus, later announced it had no deal with Cyprus Cement.
Traders said negotiations between the two companies on a merger had been on and off for some time, each time with a different scenario.
Vassiliko is on the market with a capitalisation of 64.3 million pounds, and Cyprus Cement with a capitalisation of 40 million.
"This time round it caught us unawares," one broker admitted. "This really needs to be clarified because we still don't know what is going on."
Vassiliko was trading at 160.5 on Friday. It fell at the beginning of last week but between Wednesday and Friday it jumped 11 cents. ($=0.46 cents)
